subject: Issue estimating CI with mixed mirt

messages.author: ebd1cade7d809825
messages.subject: Issue estimating CI with mixed mirt
parts:
Hi, im using the following code to estimate an Rash and 2PL models with mixedmirt:

rmod1b <- mixedmirt(it, cov[, 1:2], model, fixed = ~ 0 + items, random = ~ 1|class,
                    itemtype = "2PL")
coef(rmod1b)
But in some items i obtain the following:

$`18`
           a1      d  g  u
par     0.855 -0.201  0  1
CI_2.5    NaN -0.330 NA NA
CI_97.5   NaN -0.072 NA NA

$`19`
           a1     d  g  u
par     1.177 0.972  0  1
CI_2.5    NaN 0.812 NA NA
CI_97.5   NaN 1.132 NA NA

¿How can i fix this issue?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Issue estimating CI with mixed mirt
parts:
This is unfortunately a common issue when the ACOV matrix is estimated stochastically. The best thing to do is likely to draw more values to help stabilize the estimates. See ?mirt and locate the technical list for the element MHRM_SE_draws, and increase to something higher (like 20000+). HTH.

Phil
